properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/21/2025 to BRANCH JOHN D in Warren City, Warren county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BRANCH JOHN D
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/21/2025
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8252809
Permit API: 123-45979
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Warren City
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 10/21/2025
Comments: There was a crude oil release from inside a tank battery located next to this well that occurred during the night on October 19th or early in the morning on the 20th. Approximately 21 barrels of crude oil was discharged from one of the steel stock tanks in the battery. The operator is unsure at this time as to the exact cause of the release. He suspects a hole in the tank and plans to pressure test the tank. The release stayed inside the containment dike that surrounds the tanks.Crews were able to use vac trucks to remove the crude and fresh water was used to flush under tanks and equipment. The contaminated water was being stored inside the produced water tanks on site. Roustabouts were out this morning with oil absorbent pads catching any residual crude they could find. With more rain in the forecast Mr. Branch indicated they would be addressing any stray crude that may still be present in the coming days. The release looked largely remediated upon my arrival. The need for any additional cleanup measures will be evaluated during future inspection of this lease.

Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/25/2023
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an INCIDENT inspection of the STL Resources - Marshlands Play, State 822 Well Pad located in Gaines Twp, Tioga Co. on 5/25/23 at 1030 hours in response to notification of a release of 25 gallons of drilling mud (CID#372425) from a workover rig. The weather was 50 degrees, mostly sunny, winds NNE @15mph. Activity onsite consists of the Howard Drilling work-over rig and crew. Mr. Ken Shade and Mr. Seth Rodriguez were also present onsite from STL Resources. Lester Taylor, DEP OGI was also present onsite. The incident report states "At 7:15 p.m on 5/25/23, a 25 gallon spill of drilling mud occurred when a rotating annular seal on a work over rig failed due to an overpressure incident. The spill was confined to the gravel around the rig in an area estimated to be 10 feet by 10 feet. The spilled mud will be cleaned up by site personnel."As of today's inspection, the release appears to consists of diesel based drilling mud. The mud was sprayed from the failed annular seal in approximately a 12 foot radius around the rig. Mr. Rodriguez stated he believed 15-20 gallons of the mud was released to the pad surface. The spray appears to have spread further to the south side of the pad due to winds. STL used an excavator to remove the impacted pad material to the SE of the workover rig. The material was placed in a half round container located on secondary containment for disposal. Secondary containment was observed in placed under the rig vehicle and under the pipe delivery system but not under the rig itself or around the well cellar. This allowed the diesel based mud to be released to the pad surface under the rig in an approximately 12' x 20' area. Mr. Rodriguez stated they would not be able to complete removal of the impacted pad material until the rig has completed it's work-over activities and been relocated to the next well later today. Mr. Rodriguez provided an email update at 1836 hours stating the impacted pad area had been successfully remediated. STL Resources revised the estimate the diesel based drilling mud released outside of containment to ~10 gallons. The impacted area was approximately 448 sq ft with an additional 176 sq ft impacted by mist. Approximately 5 cubic yards (10 tons) of material was removed from the site. Violations of the following regulations are cited against the 1H well API#117-20741 as IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED : CSL 402(b) and 25 Pa Code 78a.64(c)(1)I departed the site at 1330 hours.

properties.content:

Violation ID: 8174744
Permit API: 027-21517
Unconventional: Yes
County: Centre
Municipality: Burnside Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/08/2024
Comments: Rick Hall of EQT reported a spill to the Department on 2/6/24. Mr. Hall reported that during the plugging operation of well 027-21517 on 1/23/24, they were flowing the well to a gas buster and a spray/mist came out of the gas buster. It was estimated as 3 gallons at the time so it wasnt reported to DEP at that time. They scraped it up.On 2/5/24, they discovered that since 1/23/24, things have warmed up, there has been melting, and they discovered water that had elevated conductivity. They scraped some additional material and found that the spill is deeper than originally expected. I conducted an incident inspection on 2/8/24 with Bo Hampson of EQT. According to Mr. Hampson, all impacted materials have been scraped up and removed from the site. Evaluated readings were found under the gas buster so for now, the operator has installed additional containment on both sides of the gas buster. Once the plugging operation is ceased, they will remove the gas buster, containment, and further investigate the impacted area. I conducted field screenings on various spots near the gas buster and throughout the well pad using a Hanna Gro Line Soil probe. Readings ranged from 0.01 mS/cm to 0.62 mS/cm near the gas buster. I was unable to screen right next to the gas buster due to additional containment. Please contact notify me when the gas buster will be removed from the site so I can conduct additional screenings. The Department recommends that the operator pursue Act 2 due to the unknown volume. Violations have been cited.

Comments: On 8/20/21 OGI J. Branan conducted a follow up inspection on PGE 37-063-31807 Marjorie C Yanity 1025 OG well. The water in the cellar is below the 11-3/4¿ x 16¿ casing. The gas bubbling is not visible due to the water level being below the top of the 11 ¿ ¾¿ by 16¿ casing annulus at the time of the inspection. Based on gas samples taken by Moody & Associates, and evaluation by ECHELON Applied Geosciences Consulting evaluations and interpretations, the gas is identified as lower Mississippian. ¿The gas in the 11-3/4¿ X 16¿ of the Yanity 1025 is likely associated with Lower Mississippi Formations in this area of the basin, possibly the Burgoon (Big Injun) sands.¿ (ECHELON Applied Geosciences Consulting) The Burgoon sands are approximately 400¿ to 500¿ deep. After reviewing ECHELONs evaluations and interpretations, and PGE 37-063-31807 1025 well completion report. Several coal seams and a couple freshwater aquafers were encountered before the casing seat of the surface string. There are freshwater aquafers noted on the well completion report at 83¿ and 130¿ and coal at 27¿ 83¿ 127¿ 152¿ 155¿ and 338¿. The depth of 11-3/4¿ casing is at 568.6¿, a couple hundred feet below the deepest coal. The report identifies the gas source behind the surface casing and a potential to comingle with the identified water aquifers. The Department is denying PGE any request to vent the gas from the 11-3/4¿ x 16¿ annulus as a permeant repair solution. As per 78.86 PGE is required to submit a plan to remediate the issue and has failed to do so. Also, within 30 days of receiving the inspection report, the Department is requesting any Logs or previous predrill data associated with the well.

Permit API: 051-24464
Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Compliance Schedule Evaluation
Inspection Date: 12/30/2025
Comments: On December 30, 2025, an on-site meeting was held with operator representative Brad Daugherty to discuss outstanding violations and provide clarifications that have been requested in previous inspection reports. This is also a follow-up inspection to IR 4113942. A violation was issued in IR 4088070 for failure to restore the well site by 10/30/2025, in accordance with the 5/01/2025 amendment of the 12/16/2021 CO and A. The Department requested an NOV Response to IR 4088070 from the operator by December 4, 2025.The First Modification to the COA was entered on 5/01/2025. Paragraph 3i of the 12/16/2021 CO and A states: "M4 shall immediately commence work to completely restore the Well sites upon execution of the First Amendment and complete restoration of the Well Sites by October 30, 2025, in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas act, 58 Pa.C.S. 3216, the site restoration regulations set forth in 25 Pa. Code 78a.65, and all applicable provisions of the Clean Streams Law and the regulations promulgated thereunder. M4 shall submit form 8000 PM-OOGN0075, "Well Site Restoration Report," within sixty (60) days of restoring the Well Sites." Site restoration is to be conducted "as closely to original conditions as practicable, including restoration of original contours and capability of supporting land uses existing prior to drilling of the Well(s) by October 30, 2025, unless M4 obtains a signed and notarized written consent of the landowner to leave the Well Site in an altered state".The following was observed:Upon arrival, Daugherty presented a copy of the expired ESCGP for this site, which contains the site restoration plans. They are to be stored on site in a weatherproof storage box (photo 1). Daugherty also reported that the contractor who conducted site reclamation possessed a copy of the site restoration on site during the time of IR 4088070. Daugherty proceeded to explain that the operator did not install the super silt fence north of the well site, and reported that its existence was documented before site reclamation (photo 4). Although site stabilization and progress of restoration could not be completely evaluated during this inspection due to the snow cover, it is still evident through the snow cover that the site has not attained greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth (photos 5, 8, and 9). Daugherty stated that reapplication of mulch and seed is tentatively scheduled for January 1, 2026; weather permitting.Based on observations from this inspection, the violation issued in IR 4088070 shall remain outstanding.

Report Details

Violation ID: 8268426
Permit API: 035-21178
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/26/2026
Comments: On March 26, 2026, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident site inspection at the EQT ARO LLC COP Tract 343 Pad C. On March 25, 2026, at 1526, EQT reported a spill of drilling mud outside of containment onto the well pad surface to the DEP spill hotline. Coastal Rig 103 is onsite conducting plugging operations on the C1015H Well. The plugging rig had moved onsite on Monday, March 23, 2026. Prior to the plugging rig being onsite a snubbing rig was located onsite. When the plugging rig mobilized to the site, large water puddles from recent rain covered some of the well pad. Once the puddles dried, an area approximately 40 feet by 20 feet was noticed to the north of the rig containment. DEP spoke with Tobias Excavating and he said that last evening he tested the impacted area with a PID meter and did not return elevated results on the meter. Tobias said Matt Locke with Tuscarora Geologic and Environmental Services screened the area last evening with a conductivity meter and did not return elevated results on the meter. DEP spoke with EQT Rick Hall on the phone while onsite and EQT thinks drilling mud was sprayed while the snubbing rig was onsite and the spill did not reveal itself until the water onsite dried up. Mr. Hall estimates approximately 25 gallons of drilling mud was spilled outside of containment onto the well pad surface. At the time of inspection, Tobias had already scraped up the impacted area and placed the impacted soil into rolloff dumpsters. Approximately, an inch to three inches of stone and soil were scraped up to remove the impacted material. While conducting the inspection, Tobias was spreading top stone on the area that was scraped up. The spilling of drilling mud outside of containment onto the well pad surface is a violation of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. Due to the immediate response to clean up the spill the violations are consider to be immediately corrected.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/13/2021 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in Nicholson Twp, Fayette county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/13/2021
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 933245
Permit API: 051-23196
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Nicholson Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/13/2021
Comments: Inspection conducted in response to a complaint received by the Department of corroded production tanks and possible leak. Arrived on-site at approx. 1130 to conduct investigation. Well appeared equipped for production. No well label was observed on any of the production equipment on site. Recommend Operator affix permanent well label IAW the regulations. Well posting was present but has the wrong permit number on posting (Photo 3). Recommend Operator re-post with the appropriate and correct information for this well. Background conductance reading was taken in a field west of well pad (Photo 1). Conductance value in this location was 170 micro Siemens. Heavy corrosion was observed on production tanks. Holes have developed along the south and west sides of tank (Photos 2/4/5/8/9/10). A large hole (2'x2') has developed on the west side of tank. Production fluid/brine observed approx. 3" below large hole (Photo 5). Conductance of liquid in tank was 14,500 micro Siemens (Photo 6). Tank was located within earthen berm. Conductance readings were taken along the ground on the south and south-west sides of tank (Photos 4 & 8). Values were 3,740 & 4,510 micro Siemens respectively. These values were well above the background conductance reading and indicate a release of production fluid/brine onto the ground. Request Operator determine and provide quantity of release, the method how the quantity was determined, and the duration of the release. Recommend the Operator immediately remove all production fluid/brine from the production tank for proper disposal. It is also recommended that this production tank be removed and impacted soils beneath/adjacent to tank be delineated and areas impacted remediated. Production tank should be replaced once remediation is completed and confirmed by both the Operator and Department. NOTE: Conductance readings taken along the earthen berm were at background. It does not appear at this time that the release has migrated laterally. Violations are being cited related to the release of fluids to the ground and well label/posting. Pending Operator's response, additional violations may be cited.

Comments: On 7/12/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Chesapeake Folta well site. It was 79 degrees and clear when I arrived on location. Precision drilling rig 573 has finished drilling four new wells at the site. The rig and drilling equipment have been removed from the site. The four new wells have not been completed yet. The department received stimulation notifications for the four new wells on 7/12/2023. The six existing wells remain shut in for the duration of the drilling and completion process. Vent lines were connected to each of the six existing wells, venting into two totes. The Hattie N3H was off-gasing into a tote at the time of the inspection.While at the site, I met with Chesapeake's company man, Rudy Smith, who explained current operations as follows: The frac fleet is expected to start arriving tomorrow and fracking operations on the first well are expected to start on 7/15/2023. A temporary waterline has been installed that will bring water for the fracking operations; the water will be pulled from the Salsman SWW on the Susquehanna River. I was unaccompanied during the site inspection. 17 350-barrel tanks were located on site in two separate secondary containment structures. The freshwater AST has been installed on the northwest corner of the pad. There was a gas buster frac tank and a rolloff dumpster on site. The dumpster was marked as residual waste and did have a liner in it. Secondary containment was in place around the wellheads and on a portion of the center of the pad. I field tested water on the unprotected pad surface with results at 0.4 S conductance or less. I also tested water inside the secondary containments with results at 0.2 mS conductance or less.Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM has not been installed at the site. A new ESG3 was issued for the site on 5/4/2023. Construction on the ESG3 structures has not been initiated yet.Violations cited in inspection report 3520104 on 3/15/2023 are still outstanding for the site for elevated conductance fluid discovered on the unprotected pad surface after drilling operations had been completed.The DEP recommends that Chesapeake uses good chemical handling practices at the site and clean up any spilled chemical as soon as it is discovered.I left the site at 1055 hours.

Violation ID: 916952
Permit API: 117-22080
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Liberty Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/12/2021
Comments: An incident inspection was conducted after the operator reported a release of an estimated 20 gallons of produced water to the pad surface. The operator stated in the notification that a stain was observed on the pad surface on 5/11/21 in a load off area in front of a battery of tanks. This led to the discovery of high conductivity fluid on the pad in this area. The initial electrical conductivity readings of the fluid on the pad were between 15 to 20 mS/cm according to the operator's notification. I met with Matt Tusing of Penn E&R upon arriving on location. The area in front of a frac tank battery where the release occurred was taped off. The area has been excavated but not yet backfilled. No fluid was present in this area or in the adjacent secondary containment. No puddles were observed in other areas on the pad. The water in the stormwater controls adjacent to the pad had electrical conductivity readings of less than 1000 uS/cm. Matt Tusing said that the pad surface had soil electrical conductivity readings of less than 2000 uS/cm after excavating the area of the release. He said that approximately half of a half-round roll-off box was filled with the excavated material. The approximate area of the pad excavated was 45 ft by 45 ft. He also said that the secondary containment for the tanks was pulled back and the EC of the soil there was lower which led them to believe that the produced water did not get under the tanks. No evidence of remaining produced water was observed on the pad. Violations noted and considered immediately corrected.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/17/2021 to ARD OPR LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: ARD OPR LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/17/2021
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 920803
Permit API: 081-21885
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 6/17/2021
Comments: This admin inspection is in response to the receipt of partial analytical results for sample number 0718-177, taken on 6/7/21 as part of inspection number 3202448 on Pad B. Elevated strontium and aluminum in the analytical results indicate the release of a pollutional substance. In a call on 6/10/21 between Sean Vanfleet, DEP WQSS, and Rick Hall, representative for ARD, Mr. Hall said that there had previously been a tank containing brine on Pad B while the drilling operation was rigging up. He stated he found out from site personnel that the tank had leaked and released an estimated 20 barrels of brine onto secondary containment. Mr. Hall said that the berms on the secondary containment were not fully installed at that time and the fluid ran toward the area of the pad surface where sample 0718-177 was taken. Mr. Hall said that Creston Environmental screened the pad and found elevated conductivity in the travel lane where sample 0718-177 was taken. He said that the pad surface was scraped down to a depth of approximately 1" in this area. He said 3 boxes were filled with the excavated material. He stated that fluid with an elevated conductivity continued to seep out from beneath the secondary containment so a sump has been installed to collect this fluid. The remainder of the pad was also screened by Creston according to Rick. Creston also took a sample from the same area where sample 0718-177 was taken. Mr. Hall said that the company man did not initially report the release from the tank as he believed that the fluid had stayed on the secondary containment. Based on the estimated release volume, the Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation. Violations noted. Outstanding violations noted.

Inspection Date: 3/21/2023
Comments: On 3/21/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine site inspection at the Chesapeake Stoorza well site. This inspection was to assess the condition of the storage piles of excavated contaminated material that was transported from the Chesapeake Grippo well site. It was 50 degrees and clear when I arrived on location. There are three piles of excavated material on the pad surfaces. The south pile is estimated at 60' x 100' x 12' tall. The northeast pile is estimated at 40' x 50' x 12' tall. The northwest pile is estimated at 40' x 50' x 15' tall. The three piles are stationed in secondary containment with a plastic liner protected by a fabric liner. The piles are covered with a plastic liner. I did witness a separation to the plastic cover on the south pile. I also witnessed a separation to the berm wall on the north side of the south pile. There was visible damage to the plastic secondary containment liner on the south side of the northeast pile.In close proximity to the excavation piles, I field tested water puddles on the unprotected pad surface fir conductivity with an Oakton PCTS 50 with the following results: A 12' x 6' water puddle on the unprotected pad surface at the north edge of the southeast excavated material pile field tested at 3.18 mS conductance. A 3' x 2' water puddle on the south side of the northwest pile of excavated material field tested at 5.44 mS conductance. A 3' x 12' water puddle that was approximately a half inch deep on the unprotected pad surface on the south side of the northwest excavated material pile field tested at over 20 mS conductance. A 20' x 15' water puddle along the east side of the northeast pile of excavated material field tested at 4.36 mS conductance.No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. The site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM is addressed by three retentive grading/infiltration areas that are adequately stabilized and functioning as designedThere were two wells staged for production. Both wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. The GPUs and production tank had secondary containment.The release of an unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid to the pad surface is a violation of CSL 402(b). The failure to contain regulated substances within secondary containment is a violation of 78a.64a(b). The DEP recommends the following:1. Due to the elevated conductance fluid discovered on the unprotected pad surface, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 due to the unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid impacting the unprotected pad surface. 2. Assess the condition of the excavated piles secondary containments and repair as necessary.3. Recommend daily monitoring of the site until waste is removed.I left the site at 1650 hours.

Violation ID: 8210684
Permit API: 051-24210
Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 12/04/2024
Comments: On December 4 2024, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in regards to the spill and associated violations issued under inspection report 3853723.The findings are as follows:At the time of this inspection, the Act 9 sign was posted at the access road entrance and the road appeared stabilized with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) as well as the Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan (PPC) was in the on site mailbox located at the entrance to the well pad.It appears remediation has begun as soil appears to be excavated from the areas previously identified by the Department and operator to be contaminated. Plastic lining appeared to be placed on all areas of excavation. Temporary erosion and sediment controls appeared installed and functioning correctly downslope of the excavation.The Department was unable to obtain conductivity readings in the areas covered by the plastic lining, however readings were taken just under the lining adjacent to the well head and downslope where no lining was covering the ground. Conductivity readings taken just under the lining adjacent to the well head indicated that not all contaminated material has been removed with readings of 3.17mS, 2.65mS, and 3.14mS. The conductivity reading taken in the area downslope with no plastic lining was 0.25mS, which is comparable to the background reading taken of 0.26mS.Based on the conductivity readings obtained during today's inspection, it does not appear all contaminated materials have been removed from the well site. The Department recommends the operator reassess the well site and ensure all contaminated materials are removed. The Department also recommends the operator ensure the site is properly temporarily stabilized if earth disturbance work ceases for 4 or more days.Based on today's inspection, violations remain outstanding.

Permit API: 083-47442
Unconventional: No

Municipality: Hamilton Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/09/2026
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to being notified by Chuck Rippey of Copperhead Enterprises on 7/8/26 of a crude oil spill due to a compromised subsurface gathering line located at the entrance of the spur road that accesses this conventional well. At the time of notification, according to Chuck, all wells on the lease had been shut in and containment measures were being placed throughout the impacted area.At the onset of this inspection, I met with Chuck who explained that the gathering line failed due to valves on the gathering lines at the tank battery unknowingly being closed by a suspected, unknown, third party prior to the lease being pumped on the afternoon of 7/8/26. It is estimated that the wells on the lease were pumping for 2-3 hours before the well tender drove towards this well and noticed the release at approximately 15:00. After ceasing production and shutting in the wells, Chuck reported the release to this WQSS via telephone.At the origin of the release, crude oil had sprayed onto the road bank and lower limbs of nearby trees. The majority of the crude oil migrated west/ northwest in a roadside ditch alongside Chappel Fork Road for approximately 400' before reaching a spring run that evolves into an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Chappel Fork. Pockets of crude oil were observed in the spring run/UNT between where it intersects Chappel Fork Road and its confluence with Chappel Fork. Crude oil was also present in an approximate 750' stretch of Chappel Fork downslope of the stream's confluence with the aforementioned spring run/UNT.At this time, underflow dams, absorbent booms and pads have been placed throughout the impacted portions of the roadside ditch, spring run/UNT and Chappel Fork to contain the released product. Crews were in the process of recovering crude that was collecting behind the various containment measures and replacing saturated absorbents as needed. I advised Chuck to continue the ongoing practices and to place additional booms in slow moving water to minimize the potential for further migration downstream. After further progress is made with recovering the free crude, Chuck intends to excavate the contaminated soil at the origin of the release and replace the ruptured portion of the gathering line.At this time, the quantity of crude oil that was released is unknown. Chuck intends to stage the excavated contaminated soil on a lined pod at this well site until proper disposal at a landfill is arranged. Documentation of this disposal and confirmatory sampling of the impacted area after its remediation is expected to be provided to the Department in order for this incident to be considered closed.Upcoming inspections will be done throughout the remediation of this release to ensure suitable progress is being made.

At the time of notification, according to Chuck, all wells on the lease had been shut in and containment measures were being placed throughout the impacted area.At the onset of this inspection, I met with Chuck who explained that the gathering line failed due to valves on the gathering lines at the tank battery unknowingly being closed by a suspected, unknown, third party prior to the lease being pumped on the afternoon of 7/8/26. It is estimated that the wells on the lease were pumping for 2-3 hours before the well tender drove towards this well and noticed the release at approximately 15:00. After ceasing production and shutting in the wells, Chuck reported the release to this WQSS via telephone.At the origin of the release, crude oil had sprayed onto the road bank and lower limbs of nearby trees. The majority of the crude oil migrated west/ northwest in a roadside ditch alongside Chappel Fork Road for approximately 400' before reaching a spring run that evolves into an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Chappel Fork. Pockets of crude oil were observed in the spring run/UNT between where it intersects Chappel Fork Road and its confluence with Chappel Fork. Crude oil was also present in an approximate 750' stretch of Chappel Fork downslope of the stream's confluence with the aforementioned spring run/UNT.At this time, underflow dams, absorbent booms and pads have been placed throughout the impacted portions of the roadside ditch, spring run/UNT and Chappel Fork to contain the released product. Crews were in the process of recovering crude that was collecting behind the various containment measures and replacing saturated absorbents as needed. I advised Chuck to continue the ongoing practices and to place additional booms in slow moving water to minimize the potential for further migration downstream. After further progress is made with recovering the free crude, Chuck intends to excavate the contaminated soil at the origin of the release and replace the ruptured portion of the gathering line.At this time, the quantity of crude oil that was released is unknown. Chuck intends to stage the excavated contaminated soil on a lined pod at this well site until proper disposal at a landfill is arranged. Documentation of this disposal and confirmatory sampling of the impacted area after its remediation is expected to be provided to the Department in order for this incident to be considered closed.Upcoming inspections will be done throughout the remediation of this release to ensure suitable progress is being made.

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 892781
Permit API: 081-21794
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Jackson Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 08/26/2020
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a report of a release discovered by the operator on August 22, 2020. DEP EP specialist Justin Abbott accompanied me on this inspection and we were met by Mike Deming of SWN on site. According to Mr. Deming, fluid was found between the layers of the secondary containment near where the blender had been during the recent frac. He said that the containment was removed in this area and puddles of fluid with elevated conductivity (EC) were discovered on the pad surface. He said that a spill of 10 gallons of produced water had been spilled on the secondary containment during the frac in this area and he believed that this release was related. At the time of this inspection, the area impacted by the release had already been excavated. The EC readings in this area on the Hanna soil conductivity meter were all less than 1 mS/cm. Mr. Deming said that approximately 60 tons of material had been excavated in an area approximately 60 ft x 80 ft. He estimated the spill volume at 10 gallons based on this information. Some puddles with EC ranging between 2 to 3 mS/cm were observed on the pad. The puddles were located in travel lanes on the pad. Mr. Deming said that he believed that these were due to the truck traffic bringing magnesium chloride onto the pad because magnesium chloride is used for dust control on the access road. The Department recommends sucking up these puddles as needed.Violations noted and considered immediately corrected.

Comments: Responded to a call from Minard Run to Scott Motter ( Dep representative) in regards that there had been a crude oil spill at one of there tank batteries in Forest County, Howe Township PA. Upon arriving on location I met with Minard Run Representative Gary Davis and USFS Mike Lewis. They gave a brief run down of the incident and work that had been completed to stop the flow of Crude Oil. There was a failure at well 053-27124. A valve broke which was connected to a steel line on the exit side of the check valve, which is going to tank battery. Minard Run is on site. A new valve was installed. Booms and pads were in place at the time of my arrival. They are Currently digging diversion ditches and a siphon dam. Crude product left the well site, traveled the road ditch, and went through a culvert. At that point some of the product went into a fresh water pond and some oil diverted around the pond into a wet land and then into a wooded area. Once it entered the wooded area the product penetrated the large rock structure area and flowed underground to the fresh water tributary. Pictures show where Minard Run placed booms to attempt to stop the flow down stream. The flow is carrying some product further down stream, in which they have more booms in place. It was approx estimate of 2 to 3 barrels of crude leaked. Minard Run was going to try to get a volume of the gathering lines to help identify the volume. It was suggested to add additional booms down stream and continue with the current clean up process. In light of future rains tonight it was suggested to leave booms in-place and remove pads to prevent them being pushed down stream. Minard Run did an excellent job responding and attempting to clean up the oil in the early stages of the incident. This will be forwarded to WQS for follow up.

Inspection Type: Site Restoration
Inspection Date: 9/23/2025
Comments: On September 23, 2025, the DEP conducted an inspection at the Schwotzer Arthur well site. This inspection was conducted in response to a Post-Drilling Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR) that was submitted by the operator on August 6, 2025 for well 6H (125-29133). A notarized Landowner Waiver of Well Site Restoration was submitted with the WSRR, as sound walls currently remain onsite. Total Depth was obtained on November 17, 2024 according to the Well Record, therefore site restoration is to be complete by August 17, 2025.An Erosion and Sediment (E and S) individual permit (ESP07632300100E) was issued by the DEP for this site on January 26, 2024 and expires on January 25, 2029.The following was observed:Accumulated fine sediment from the access road was observed in the rock-lined channel along Rural Valley Road (photo 3). This sedimentation has not reached the storm culvert where it empties (photo 4). No accelerated erosion rills were observed on the access road and well pad at the time of inspection (photos 2, 9, and 21). Exposed soil was observed in several areas onsite which appear to require additional temporary stabilization (photos 6 and 19). The soil crack that was present on the southwestern fill slope of the well pad appears to be repaired. Riprap has been added to this location to improve drainage (photo 12). No toe bulge was observed below at the time of inspection. Repair work has been conducted on the slough that occurred on the well pad cutslope, with no loose sediment observed in the vegetated channel below (photos 14-18). What appears to be surface cracking was observed at the top of well pad cut slope (photo 20). This appears to be due to recent excessive dryness onsite. No toe bulge was observed belowThe Act 9 sign is fully visible at the entrance of the access road, in accordance with 78a.55 (photo 1). The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (photo 22). The GPU units onsite are equipped with interconnected drip pans (photo 23). This form of GPU secondary containment was approved by the DEP for use on 6/21/2022. Well 6H is equipped with a well tag and appears to be in production (photo 24). No evidence of fluid leaks to the ground around it was observed. There are six additional well heads onsite that also appear to be equipped for production. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan, Well permits, Individual E and S permit approval letter, E and S permit drawings, and E and S inspection log are onsite (photo 25). The ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the information required by 78a.55.Based on observations from this inspection, the WSRR is denied. Because the well site is not exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth, violations are being issued for failure to restore 9 months post-drilling.While the DEP was onsite, Jessica Ullom from Range Resources arrived onsite. The DEP spoke with Ullom to inform them of the forthcoming recommendations in this inspection report.The DEP recommends that the access road is maintained in a manner that prevents fine sediment from accumulating further in stormwater discharge areas, including by conducting maintenance in accordance with the access road cross section shown on page C134 of site permit plans. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending further assessment and evaluation in a future follow up inspection.The DEP also recommends that the operator assess and evaluate the site and implement temporary stabilization where exposed soil is found. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending further assessment and evaluation in a future follow up inspection. Finally, the DEP recommends that the operator assess and evaluate the soil cracking at the top of the well pad cutslope to determine whether it threatens site stability or is due to recent dry conditions, and that the operator notify the DEP of findings.

Comments: Pressure Buildup Tests (PBUT) were conducted for 72 hours from 4/29/2022 through 5/2/2022 at the seven gas wells drilled in 2021/2022 at the Cruttenden 846 pad. Comments: On 8/12/25 at 10:00 AM, I arrived at the Kovalish 1 in Derry Twp, Westmoreland county. The department performed a follow up inspection of the KOVALISH 1 OG well. Permit number# 129-24618. Related to open violations from Inspection reports #3936896, #3645422, #3839972, #3927515. At the time of inspection: The well is considered abandoned and was observed shut in and disconnected. Violations 78.91(a) and OGA3220(A) are being continued. And all the necessary equipment for production remains removed from the site. The disconnected electrical service and the disconnected associated pipelines that are exposed make the site appear to have had an electric powered gas compressor on location sometime ago. There is a damaged/crooked 2"ball valve on a disconnected line, no gas was detected at this area or any other area onsite during the inspection. The Mechanical Integrity Assessments and Annual Production Reports have been submitted and are up to date. Although, no production has been reported after regulatory inactive status had expired on 05/20/2022 to the date of inspection 02/13/2025. No spills or gas leaks were observed. The well exhibited a high degree of corrosion of the surface production tubing. Although, no gas was detected leaking from the area. An operator posting and well tag are present.
